note: Open CodeQL alerts on main. A ratchet in BOTH directions: a rise fails, and so does a fall, because a baseline nobody lowers stops describing the tree. Lower it in the commit that fixes or dismisses the alert. Every count here is untriaged work, not an accepted level. Two things this gate cannot see, both worth carrying between readings. It compares severity BUCKETS, so alerts leaving and alerts arriving in the same bucket net off against each other and an arrival is reported as no rise at all — a falling total is not evidence that nothing was introduced. And a dismissal binds to an alert NUMBER rather than to a finding: when a code change moves a finding, the analysis can close the old number and mint a new one, which drops the dismissal and puts an already-ruled-on finding back into this count as though it were new work. Before treating a number as new, check whether it is an older one relocated — same rule, same file, and an old fixed_at equal to the new created_at. The By rule table in the run summary is the only place either shows, and nothing gates on it.
